name: Neuromorphic and optical hardware
blurb: Breakdown cover for architectures with no established failure statistics.
summary: Breakdown cover for architectures with no established failure statistics.

part_3_high_value_red_flags: An exclusion for inherent vice or latent defect that would bar coverage for design flaws in the novel neuromorphic architecture.
A wear and tear exclusion that would exclude the gradual degradation of optical components such as laser diodes and waveguides.
A sublimit for electronic data or data restoration that is too low to cover the cost of rebuilding corrupted neural network weights.
An exclusion for mysterious disappearance or unexplained loss that would defeat a claim where the failure mode cannot be identified due to lack of failure statistics.
A consequential loss exclusion that would bar business interruption coverage when the hardware breakdown causes downstream revenue loss.
An exclusion for laser or optical radiation that would remove bodily injury coverage for eye damage from a failed photonic module.
A firmware or software exclusion that would exclude breakdowns caused by a faulty update to the neuromorphic processing unit.
manuscript_wording_and_carve_backs: Delete the inherent vice and latent defect exclusions for the neuromorphic and optical hardware, replacing them with a design defect endorsement that covers sudden and accidental failure.
Add a resultant physical damage clause so that a firmware or software error that causes a hardware breakdown is covered as equipment breakdown.
Add an unscheduled equipment endorsement to cover prototype and pilot neuromorphic units that are not yet listed on the schedule.
Increase the electronic data sublimit to cover the full cost of restoring neural network weights and optical routing tables after a failure.
Add a contingent business interruption endorsement for the failure of a key supplier of photonic integrated circuits or memristor arrays.
Add a laser safety carve back to the general liability policy so that bodily injury from optical radiation is not excluded.
Negotiate an agreed value endorsement for custom optical components that have no established market value, to avoid disputes over replacement cost.

part_4_program_structure_and_limits.bi_waiting_period: The business interruption waiting period is typically 24 to 72 hours, but for hardware with no failure statistics underwriters may require a longer waiting period of 7 days to reduce frequency risk.
part_4_program_structure_and_limits.business_interruption: Business interruption coverage includes loss of income and continuing normal operating expenses, with an extended period of indemnity of 12 to 24 months to allow for replacement of custom optical components.
part_4_program_structure_and_limits.property_eb_equipment: Equipment breakdown coverage is written on a blanket basis for all scheduled neuromorphic and optical hardware, including prototype units, with a sublimit for expediting expenses and temporary replacement equipment.
part_4_program_structure_and_limits.per_occurrence_primary_excess_layered_pr: Property coverage for the neuromorphic and optical hardware is typically placed on a layered basis with a primary property policy covering physical damage and an excess property tower above it, with per occurrence limits set by the replacement cost of the most valuable single installation.

part_2_paper_type_and_limit_structure.cgl_primary: A primary commercial general liability policy with a typical limit of one million dollars per occurrence and two million dollars in the aggregate, subject to underwriting review of the product exposure.
part_2_paper_type_and_limit_structure.paper_basis: Occurrence based for the commercial general liability and products liability because the insured event is the physical failure of the neuromorphic or optical hardware, not the date a claim is reported.
part_2_paper_type_and_limit_structure.excess_umbrella_towers: Excess liability towers are built in layers above the primary, with attachment points and total limits driven by the maximum foreseeable loss from a single hardware failure event and the insured's contractual indemnity obligations.

part_1_core_third_party_liability_exposu: Product liability arising from a neuromorphic chip making an incorrect inference that causes bodily injury or property damage in a downstream application such as robotics or medical imaging.
Bodily injury from laser radiation if an optical interconnect or photonic module fails and emits uncontrolled light.
Third party property damage from a fire or electrical fault originating in the novel hardware and spreading to a customer's premises.
Data loss or corruption at a third party site caused by an unpredictable fault in the optical processing unit.
Failure of the hardware in a critical infrastructure deployment leading to business interruption losses claimed by the customer as consequential damage.
Professional liability if the insured provides design or integration services and the hardware fails due to a specification error.

underwriter_wants_to_know: What accelerated life testing or burn in data exists for the neuromorphic chips and photonic integrated circuits, given there is no field failure history.
How are optical components such as lasers, modulators and waveguides monitored for degradation, and what is the expected mean time between failures.
What redundancy or fail safe architecture is built into the system to prevent a single point of failure from causing a total breakdown.
Are firmware and software updates treated as part of the equipment breakdown exposure, and what version control and rollback procedures exist.
What is the supply chain dependency for custom optical transceivers and memristor arrays, and what lead times apply for replacement parts.
What thermal management and power stability measures protect the hardware from overheating or voltage spikes that could accelerate failure.
Has any prototype or pilot deployment experienced a failure, and what was the root cause analysis.
